subject: Banking
title: Disputing Errors on Your Report
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Disputing Errors on Your Report.

hook.text: One in three Americans has an error on their credit report. Disputes are free and legally required to be investigated.

buildup.text: Under federal law, bureaus must investigate disputes within 30 days.

discovery.text: Common errors include accounts belonging to someone else, incorrect balances, and debts that were already paid off.

twist.text: Bureaus profit from data volume, not accuracy. Fixing errors costs them money.

climax.text: Credit disputes are a consumer right that bureaus make hard to use. Persistence wins because the law is on your side.

punchline.text: One in three reports has an error. Disputes are free and legally protected.

quiz.question: How long must credit bureaus investigate a dispute?
